answer: I'd like to talk about a collection that takes up more and more space in my room every year. A collection I have gradually built up over the years is my collection of books, which has grown into something I am genuinely proud of. I now have a couple of hundred books, mostly novels and history, plus a few on business and psychology, in both Bengali and English. It started fairly innocently, with a few titles I loved, but it has since become a bit of an [[obsession]]. The very first ones were old storybooks my father bought me from a street stall when I was about twelve, and I still have every one of them. I add to it whenever I travel or come across an interesting title, so it keeps expanding steadily. My favourite time to buy is the big book fair in Dhaka every February, where I usually come home with a bag far heavier than I planned. My friends also know that a book is the safest gift for me. What I enjoy most is that each book represents a different idea, story or period of my life. There is something deeply [[satisfying]] about being surrounded by a personal library. Unlike many collections, mine is not just for display; I actually read and reread them. Honestly, my books have become almost like old friends, each with its own [[significance]]. I find the act of collecting them, and the memories attached to them, thoroughly [[rewarding]]. I think a good collection reflects who you are and what you value. I hope to keep growing mine for many years to come.

followUps.q: Where do you keep all your books?
followUps.answer: Mostly on the shelves in my room, including one I built myself. They've started spilling over onto my desk and even the floor, so I'll need more space quite soon.

followUps.q: Do you ever lend books from your collection?
followUps.answer: Yes, to close friends and my younger sister. I like sharing them, because discussing a book afterwards is half the pleasure, although I do keep a careful [[mental note]] of who has what.

note: Added what the collection contains, how it began (storybooks from his father) and how he adds to it (the February book fair in Dhaka, gifts).
